  • Same base when dividing: SUBTRACT the exponents.
  • Same exponent when dividing: DIVIDE the bases.
  • Check example: 5^11 ÷ 5^8 = 5³ = 125, and (20)³ ÷ (4)³ = 5³ = 125 too.
  • x^10 ÷ x⁴ = x^6 and x⁴ ÷ y⁴ = (x/y)⁴.

mcqs.why: The base is the same, so subtract the exponents: 7 − 4 = 3. Then 5³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. This is the division law.
Subtract the exponents: 5 − 2 = 3, giving (5/7)³. Its value is 125/343, since 5³ = 125 and 7³ = 343.
Subtract the exponents: 6 − 2 = 4, giving (1/2)⁴. That equals 1/16. Keep the base 1/2 the same.
With the same base x, subtract the exponents: 10 − 4 = 6. So x^10 ÷ x⁴ = x^6. Division means subtraction of exponents, not division of them.
The exponent 5 is the same, so divide the bases: 10 ÷ 2 = 5. Then 5^5 = 3125. Keep the exponent and divide the bases.
Divide the bases: (−7) ÷ (−5) = 7/5, with exponent 4. So the value is (7/5)⁴ = 2401/625, since 7⁴ = 2401 and 5⁴ = 625.
Subtract the exponents: 6 − 5 = 1. Any number to the power 1 is itself, so the answer is 7/11.

mcqs.q: x⁴ ÷ y⁴ = ?
mcqs.why: The exponent 4 is the same for both, so divide the bases and keep the exponent: x⁴ ÷ y⁴ = (x/y)⁴. This is the second division rule.
First (2/5) ÷ (3/5) = 2/3, with exponent 6 kept. So we get (2/3)^6 = 64/729, since 2^6 = 64 and 3^6 = 729.

mcqs.q: 5^11 ÷ 5^8 equals which of these?
mcqs.why: 5^11 ÷ 5^8 = 5³ = 125. Also (20)³ ÷ (4)³ = (20/4)³ = 5³ = 125. Both sides are equal, as shown in the checking question.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.4 — Power Law, Negative and Zero Exponents
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

A power of a power means a power inside brackets with another power outside, like (5²)^7. We also learn negative exponents and the zero exponent in this exercise.

Formula / Rule

Power law: (a^m)^n = a^(m×n) — multiply the exponents.

Negative exponent: a^(−m) = 1/a^m, and 1/a^m = a^(−m).

Zero exponent: a^0 = 1 for any non-zero a, e.g. (−3)^0 = 1.

Worked Example

Simplify (5²)^7.

Step 1: Keep the base 5.

Step 2: Multiply the exponents: 2 × 7 = 14.

Step 3: So (5²)^7 = 5^14.

Another example: (1/3)^(−7) = 3^7 = 2187, because a negative exponent flips the fraction.

Positive or Negative?

A negative base with an even exponent (even negative, like −26 or −100) is positive. With an odd exponent it stays negative. Examples: (−7)^6 is positive, (−11/2)^17 is negative, (−1/5)^(−26) is positive.

Remember

  • Power of a power: MULTIPLY the exponents, e.g. (x^5)^20 = x^100.
  • 1/2^5 = 2^(−5) and 5^(−8) = 1/5^8.
  • Flipping helps: 1/(4/5)^6 = (4/5)^(−6) = (5/4)^6.
  • Any number to power 0 equals 1.

mcqs.why: For a power of a power, multiply the exponents: 2 × 7 = 14. So (5²)^7 = 5^14. This is the power law.
Multiply the exponents: 6 × 8 = 48. So the answer is (1/3)^48. The base 1/3 stays the same.
Multiply the exponents: 5 × 20 = 100. So (x^5)^20 = x^100. Adding 5 + 20 would be wrong here.

mcqs.q: 1/2^5 in negative exponent form is:
mcqs.why: We use the rule 1/a^m = a^(−m). So 1/2^5 = 2^(−5). The base stays 2 and the exponent becomes negative.

mcqs.q: 5^(−8) in positive exponent form is:
mcqs.why: A negative exponent means 1 over the power: 5^(−8) = 1/5^8. The value stays positive; only the position changes.
(1/3)^(−7) = 1/(1/3)^7 = 3^7. Since 3^7 = 2187, the answer is 2187. A negative exponent flips the fraction.
The base is negative but the exponent 6 is even, so the answer is positive: (−7)^6 = 7^6. Even exponents make negative bases positive.
The exponent 17 is odd, so a negative base keeps its minus sign. Therefore (−11/2)^17 is negative. Odd exponent means the sign stays negative.

mcqs.q: (−3)^0 equals:
mcqs.why: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1. So (−3)^0 = 1, which is positive. This is the zero exponent rule.

mcqs.q: {(−3/4)^20}² simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Multiply the exponents: 20 × 2 = 40, giving (−3/4)^40. Since 40 is even, this equals (3/4)^40, a positive value.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.5 — Mixing All the Exponent Laws
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

In this exercise we mix all the laws together: product law, division law, power law, negative exponents and zero exponents. Work step by step and change flipped fractions like (7/5)^10 into (5/7)^(−10) when needed.

Formula / Rule

a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(m×n), a^0 = 1.

Key trick: (b/a)^n = (a/b)^(−n). A power and its flip with opposite exponents cancel to 1.

Worked Example

Simplify {(2/3)²}³ ÷ (2/3)⁴.

Step 1: Use the power law: {(2/3)²}³ = (2/3)^6.

Step 2: Use the division law: (2/3)^6 ÷ (2/3)⁴ = (2/3)^(6−4) = (2/3)².

Step 3: Find the value: (2/3)² = 4/9.

Finding x example: 3^6 × 3⁴ = 3^x gives 3^10 = 3^x, so x = 10. When the bases are equal, the exponents must be equal.

Remember

  • (5/7)^6 × (5/7)⁴ × (7/5)^10 = (5/7)^10 × (5/7)^(−10) = (5/7)^0 = 1.
  • x^0 + x^5 × x^(−5) = 1 + 1 = 2.
  • (7/9)³ × (9/7)³ = 1, because the bases multiply to 1.
  • For {(4/7)³}^x = (4/7)^9, we get 3x = 9, so x = 3.

mcqs.why: First {(2/3)²}³ = (2/3)^6. Then divide: (2/3)^(6−4) = (2/3)² = 4/9. Use the power law first, then the division law.
Each pair multiplies to 1: (7/9 × 9/7)³ = 1³ = 1 and (11/12 × 12/11)^5 = 1^5 = 1. So the total is 1 + 1 = 2.
x^0 = 1, and x^5 × x^(−5) = x^(5−5) = x^0 = 1. So the answer is 1 + 1 = 2. Both parts equal 1.
First (7/8)^6 ÷ (7/8)⁴ = (7/8)². Then (7/8)² × (8/7)² = ((7/8) × (8/7))² = 1² = 1. The flipped bases cancel.

mcqs.q: If 3^6 × 3⁴ = 3^x, then x = ?
mcqs.why: By the product law, 3^6 × 3⁴ = 3^(6+4) = 3^10. The bases are equal, so the exponents are equal: x = 10.
The left side is (11/9)^(8−6) = (11/9)². So 2x = 2, which gives x = 1. Compare the exponents after simplifying.
By the power law, {(4/7)³}^x = (4/7)^(3x). So 3x = 9, giving x = 3. Multiply the inner exponent by x.
By the product law, the left side is (1/5)^(x+5). So x + 5 = 10, giving x = 5. Add the exponents when multiplying.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 4 — Powers: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

The review exercise mixes everything from Unit 4: base and exponent, all three laws, zero and negative exponents, positive and negative signs, and finding the value of x.

Formula / Rule

a^m × a^n = a^(m+n); a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n); (a^m)^n = a^(m×n); a^0 = 1.

Any number with exponent zero has value 1, e.g. 8^0 = 1 and y^0 = 1.

Worked Example

Simplify [{(2/5)²}³ ÷ (2/5)⁴] × (2/5)³.

Step 1: {(2/5)²}³ = (2/5)^6.

Step 2: (2/5)^6 ÷ (2/5)⁴ = (2/5)².

Step 3: (2/5)² × (2/5)³ = (2/5)^5 = 32/3125.

Finding x example: 25^x = 125. Write 25^x = (5²)^x = 5^(2x) and 125 = 5³, so 2x = 3 and x = 3/2.

Remember

  • Values to know: 3^5 = 243, 7⁴ = 2401, (3/4)² = 9/16, (1/4)³ = 1/64.
  • (−2)^7 is negative (odd exponent); (−3)^8 is positive (even exponent); (−5)^0 = 1 is positive.
  • 6² ÷ 3³ = 36 ÷ 27 = 4/3 — when bases and exponents are both different, find values first.
  • (3²)^5 = 3^10 = 59049 and {(−4)²}^5 = 4^10 = 1048576.

mcqs.q: In 3^5, the base and exponent are:
mcqs.why: The base is the number being multiplied, 3, and the exponent is 5. Its value is 3^5 = 243. Read the small top number as the exponent.

mcqs.q: What is 7⁴?
What is 8^0?
mcqs.why: Any number with exponent zero has value 1. So 8^0 = 1. The same rule gives y^0 = 1.
Add the exponents: 4 + 2 = 6, giving (−1/2)^6. Since 6 is even, the value is positive: 1/64.
Subtract the exponents: 7 − 4 = 3, giving 6³. Then 6³ = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216. Use the division law first, then find the value.
Multiply the exponents: 2 × 5 = 10, giving 3^10. Its value is 59049, as given in the review exercise.
The exponent 7 is odd, so a negative base stays negative. Therefore (−2)^7 is negative. Odd exponents keep the minus sign.
The exponent −10 is an even number, so the result is positive: (−8)^(−10) = 1/8^10. Even exponents, even negative ones, give positive results.
Here the bases are different, so find the values first: 6² = 36 and 3³ = 27. Then 36 ÷ 27 = 36/27 = 4/3 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: If 25^x = 125, then x = ?
mcqs.why: Write both sides with base 5: 25^x = (5²)^x = 5^(2x) and 125 = 5³. So 2x = 3, giving x = 3/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1 — Squares and Perfect Squares
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

The square of a number is the number multiplied by itself. The answer is called a perfect square. For example, the square of 2 is 2 × 2 = 4, and the square of −3 is (−3) × (−3) = 9.

From the Practical Work table: the square of 1 is 1, the square of 5 is 25, the square of −6 is 36, the square of 7 is 49, the square of 8 is 64, the square of −9 is 81, and the square of 10 is 100. Note that the square of a negative number is always positive.

Formula / Rule

Square of a = a² = a × a

A number is a perfect square if it equals n × n for some number n. The square of an even number is even, and the square of an odd number is odd.

Worked Example

Find the square of 66 and check if 95 is a perfect square.

Step 1: 66² = 66 × 66 = 4356.

Step 2: For 95, note that 9² = 81 and 10² = 100.

Step 3: 95 lies between 81 and 100 and is not the square of any whole number, so 95 is NOT a perfect square.

Squares of Fractions and Decimals

Square the top and bottom separately: (3/7)² = 9/49 and (8/9)² = 64/81. Multiply decimals by themselves: 0.5² = 0.25, 0.07² = 0.0049, 0.11² = 0.0121.

Remember

  • Squares to know: 11² = 121, 19² = 361, 25² = 625, 50² = 2500, 78² = 6084, 100² = 10000, 500² = 250000.
  • Perfect squares: 81 = 9², 121 = 11², 169 = 13², 3969 = 63². Not perfect squares: 95, 224, 3872, 9845.
  • 441 = 21² is the square of an odd number; 196 = 14², 2704 = 52² and 3600 = 60² are squares of even numbers.

mcqs.q: What is the square of 11?
mcqs.why: 11² = 11 × 11 = 121. Squaring means multiplying the number by itself once. It does not mean 11 × 2, which would give only 22.

mcqs.q: The square of −6 is:
mcqs.why: From the Practical Work table, (−6)² = (−6) × (−6) = 36. A negative number times itself gives a positive answer, so the square is 36.

mcqs.q: What is 25²?
mcqs.why: 25² = 25 × 25 = 625. Multiply the number by itself to square it. This value is also used in reverse in this unit, since √625 = 25.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a perfect square?
mcqs.why: 81 = 9 × 9 = 9², so 81 is a perfect square. The others lie between two neighbouring squares and are not perfect squares.

mcqs.q: Is 224 a perfect square?
mcqs.why: 14² = 196 and 15² = 225, so 224 lies between them. It is not the square of any whole number, so it is not a perfect square.

mcqs.q: 3969 is a perfect square because:
mcqs.why: 3969 = 63 × 63 = 63², as shown in the exercise. Checking 63² = 3969 confirms it is a perfect square.

mcqs.q: 441 = 21². 441 is the perfect square of:
mcqs.why: 441 = 21² and 21 is an odd number. So 441 is a perfect square of an odd number, and it is itself odd.
Square the numerator and the denominator separately: 3² = 9 and 7² = 49. So (3/7)² = 9/49.
0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25. Multiply the decimal by itself carefully, counting the decimal places.

mcqs.q: What is 500²?
mcqs.why: 500² = 500 × 500 = 250000. First 5 × 5 = 25, then add the four zeros from the two 500s.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2 — Square Roots by Factor Method
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

The square root of a number is the number which, multiplied by itself, gives the first number. It is the opposite of squaring. We write it with the sign √. For example, √25 = 5 because 5² = 25.

Formula / Rule

If n² = N, then √N = n. Also √(a²) = a.

Factor method: write the number as prime factors in pairs, then take one factor from each pair and multiply. For a fraction, take the square root of the numerator and denominator separately. For a decimal, write it as a fraction over 100 first.

Worked Example

Find √676 by the factor method.

Step 1: Factorise: 676 = 2 × 2 × 13 × 13 = 2² × 13².

Step 2: Take one factor from each pair: 2 × 13.

Step 3: Multiply: 2 × 13 = 26.

Step 4: Check: 26² = 676. ✓ So √676 = 26.

Fraction example: √(144/225) = 12/15 = 4/5, since √144 = 12 and √225 = 15. Decimal example: √3.24 = √(324/100) = 18/10 = 1.8.

Remember

  • Basic roots: √81 = 9, √64 = 8, √169 = 13, √484 = 22, √961 = 31, √4900 = 70.
  • Mixed numbers: first change to an improper fraction, e.g. 1 25/144 = 169/144, so the root is 13/12 = 1 1/12.
  • Decimals: √4.41 = 2.1, √6.25 = 2.5, √37.21 = 6.1, √30.25 = 5.5.
  • Always check by squaring your answer.

mcqs.why: √25 = 5 because 5² = 25. The square root is the number that gives 25 when multiplied by itself.
√81 = 9 because 9² = 81. This basic root is used again and again in this exercise.
The square root and the square cancel each other: √((49)²) = 49. In general, √(a²) = a.

mcqs.q: √676 by the factor method is:
mcqs.why: 676 = 2² × 13², so take one factor from each pair: 2 × 13 = 26. Check: 26² = 676.
484 = 2 × 2 × 11 × 11 = 2² × 11², so take one factor from each pair: √484 = 2 × 11 = 22. Check by squaring: 22² = 484.
4900 = 2² × 5² × 7², so take one factor from each pair: √4900 = 2 × 5 × 7 = 70. Check by squaring the answer: 70² = 4900.
1089 = 3 × 3 × 11 × 11 = 3² × 11², so take one factor from each pair: √1089 = 3 × 11 = 33. Check by squaring: 33² = 1089.
2304 has prime factors in pairs giving √2304 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 48. Check: 48² = 2304.
2025 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 = 3⁴ × 5², so take one factor from each pair: √2025 = 3 × 3 × 5 = 45. Check: 45² = 2025.
√144 = 12 and √225 = 15, giving 12/15, which simplifies to 4/5. Always simplify the fraction at the end.
First 1 25/144 = 169/144. Then √169 = 13 and √144 = 12, so the answer is 13/12 = 1 1/12. Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first.
√961 = 31 and √1681 = 41, so the root is 31/41. Take the root of the top and bottom separately.
Write the decimal as a fraction: 37.21 = 3721/100. Then √3721 = 61 and √100 = 10, so √37.21 = 61/10 = 6.1. Check: 6.1² = 37.21.
Write the decimal as a fraction: 30.25 = 3025/100. Then √3025 = 55 and √100 = 10, so √30.25 = 55/10 = 5.5. Check: 5.5² = 30.25.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3 — Square Roots in Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

This exercise uses square roots in daily-life word problems. When things are arranged in a square — the number of rows equals the number in each row — the number in each row is the square root of the total.

Formula / Rule

Number in each row = √(total), when rows = number in each row.

Side of a square = √(area). If length = 3 × width, then area = 3x², so find x² first, then x = √(x²).

Worked Example

784 chairs are arranged so that the chairs in each row equal the number of rows. Find the rows.

Step 1: Let the number of rows be n. Then n × n = 784, so n² = 784.

Step 2: Take the square root: n = √784 = 28.

Step 3: Check: 28² = 784. ✓

Step 4: So there are 28 rows and 28 chairs in each row.

Left-over example: 15,198 spools with 69 left over — first subtract: 15198 − 69 = 15129, then √15129 = 123 spools in each row.

Remember

  • Answers from the exercise: √2116 = 46 rows of boxes, √1681 = 41 students in each row, √625 = 25 trucks in each row, √1024 = 32 students in each row.
  • Square plot of area 240.25 m² has side √240.25 = 15.5 m.
  • Room with length 3 × width and area 720.75 m²: x² = 240.25, width = 15.5 m, length = 46.5 m.
  • Always subtract any left-over items BEFORE taking the square root.

mcqs.q: 784 chairs are arranged with rows equal to chairs in each row. How many rows are there?
mcqs.why: The number of rows is √784 = 28, since 28² = 784. So there are 28 rows with 28 chairs in each row.

mcqs.q: A square plot has area 240.25 m². The length of each side is:
mcqs.why: Side = √(area) = √240.25 = 15.5 metres, since 15.5² = 240.25. For a square, the side is the square root of the area.

mcqs.q: 2116 biscuit boxes are placed with rows equal to boxes in each row. Boxes in each row:
mcqs.why: Boxes in each row = √2116 = 46, since 46² = 2116. There are 46 rows and 46 boxes in each row.

mcqs.q: 1681 students sit with students in each row equal to the number of rows. Students in each row:
mcqs.why: Students in each row = √1681 = 41, since 41² = 1681. So there are 41 rows of 41 students.

mcqs.q: 625 trucks stand with trucks in each row equal to the number of rows. Rows:
mcqs.why: Number of rows = √625 = 25, since 25² = 625. There are 25 rows and 25 trucks in each row.

mcqs.q: 1024 students are arranged with students in each row equal to the number of rows. Rows in all:
mcqs.why: Rows = √1024 = 32, since 32² = 1024. So there are 32 rows with 32 students in each row.

mcqs.q: A room's length is 3 times its width and its area is 720.75 m². Its width and length are:
mcqs.why: Let width = x, then 3x² = 720.75, so x² = 240.25 and x = 15.5. The width is 15.5 m and the length is 3 × 15.5 = 46.5 m.

mcqs.q: A square school boundary has area 3387.24 m². One side is:
mcqs.why: Side = √3387.24 = 58.2 metres, since 58.2² = 3387.24. Take the square root of the area to get the side.

mcqs.q: 15,198 spools are arranged in a square and 69 are left over. Spools in each row:
mcqs.why: First subtract the left-over spools: 15198 − 69 = 15129. Then √15129 = 123, since 123² = 15129. Subtract before taking the root.

mcqs.q: A rectangular plot's length is 3 times its width, area 995.9052 m². Its width is:
mcqs.why: 3x² = 995.9052 gives x² = 331.9684, so x = 18.22. The width is 18.22 m and the length is 3 × 18.22 = 54.66 m.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 5 — Square Roots: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

The review mixes the whole unit: what a perfect square and a square root are, the two methods of finding a square root (factor method and division method), squares and roots of fractions and decimals, true/false facts, and word problems.

Formula / Rule

A perfect square number is the square of a number, e.g. 25 = 5². If p² = q, then p is called the square root of q.

The numbers 1, 4, 9, 16, ... are called perfect square numbers. Also √(25/36) = √25/√36 = 5/6.

Worked Example

Find √26569.

Step 1: Estimate — 160² = 25600 and 170² = 28900, so the root is between 160 and 170.

Step 2: The number ends in 9, so the root ends in 3 or 7. Try 163.

Step 3: Check: 163² = 26569. ✓

Step 4: So √26569 = 163.

Word example: a square garden of area 12100 m² has side √12100 = 110 m.

Remember

  • True/False facts: the square of an odd number is odd (so that statement calling it even is false); (4.5)² > 4.5 is true; 0.7 < (0.7)² is false because (0.7)² = 0.49.
  • Roots to know: √729 = 27, √7056 = 84, √42025 = 205, √344569 = 587, √0.0256 = 0.16, √131.1025 = 11.45.
  • 0 and 1 are the numbers whose square and square root are equal; 16 is a perfect square.
  • June spending problem: 30 days × 30 rupees = 900, so √900 = 30 rupees per day.

mcqs.q: What is a perfect square number?
options: A number that is the square of a number
mcqs.why: A perfect square number is a number that is the square of another number. For example, 25 = 5², so 25 is a perfect square number.

mcqs.q: The two methods of finding a square root are:
mcqs.why: The book gives two methods for finding a square root: (1) the factor method and (2) the division method. Both give the same answer.

mcqs.q: The square of 31 is:
mcqs.why: 31² = 31 × 31 = 961, as in the fill-in-the-blank question. This is the same fact used in reverse in Exercise 5.2, where √961 = 31.

mcqs.q: 1, 4, 9, 16, ... are called:
mcqs.why: 1 = 1², 4 = 2², 9 = 3² and 16 = 4², so these are perfect square numbers. Each one is a number multiplied by itself.
Take the roots separately: √25 = 5 and √36 = 6. So √(25/36) = 5/6, as in the fill-in-the-blank question.

mcqs.q: If p² = q, then p is called the ______ of q.
mcqs.why: If p² = q, then p is called the square root of q. This is the book's own multiple-choice question, and square root is the correct term.

mcqs.q: The numbers whose square and square root are equal are:
mcqs.why: 0² = 0 and √0 = 0, and 1² = 1 and √1 = 1. So 0 and 1 are the numbers whose square and square root are equal.

mcqs.q: Which statement is TRUE?
options: The square of an odd number is even
mcqs.why: (4.5)² = 20.25, which is greater than 4.5, so this statement is true. The others are false: odd squares are odd, (0.7)² = 0.49 < 0.7, and 25/49 < 5/7.
√7056 = 84 because 84² = 7056. This large-number root is from the review exercise.

mcqs.q: A square garden has area 12100 m². Its side is:
mcqs.why: Side = √12100 = 110 metres, since 110² = 12100. For any square, side equals the square root of the area.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1 — Continued Ratio and Sharing in a Ratio
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

A continued ratio joins two or more ratios into one ratio, like A : B : C. To join them, make the common letter have the SAME number in both ratios.

We also use ratios to share money or amounts: add all the ratio parts, find the value of one part, then multiply.

Formula / Rule

To join A : B and B : C, make the B numbers equal using the LCM, then write A : B : C

One share = total amount ÷ sum of ratio terms; each share = its ratio term × one share

In a proportion a : b = c : d, the product of the extremes equals the product of the means, so we can cross-multiply to find x

Worked Example

Question: Divide 2000 rupees among Saleem, Irfan and Imran in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5.

Step 1: Add the ratio terms: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.

Step 2: Find one share: 2000 / 10 = 200 rupees.

Step 3: Saleem gets 2 × 200 = 400 rupees.

Step 4: Irfan gets 3 × 200 = 600 rupees.

Step 5: Imran gets 5 × 200 = 1000 rupees.

Other Question Types in This Exercise

  • Simple join: A : B = 2 : 5 and B : C = 5 : 4 gives A : B : C = 2 : 5 : 4, because B is already 5 in both.
  • Join needing LCM: A : B = 3 : 7 and B : C = 8 : 9 gives 24 : 56 : 63. Weights example: Shazia : Nazia : Madiha = 40 : 72 : 99.
  • Four-part ratios: A : B : C : D can be 56 : 84 : 105 : 150. Property example: Father : Mother : Daughter : Son = 45 : 18 : 24 : 28.
  • Finding x: x : 2 = 5 : 6 gives 6x = 10, so x = 5/3.
  • Big sharing: 27,400 rupees in the ratio 70 : 28 : 21 : 18 gives gas 14,000, water 5,600, electricity 4,200 and phone 3,600 rupees.

Remember

  • Always check your sharing answers add back to the total.
  • The common letter must be made equal BEFORE joining the ratios.
  • Book prices example: 675 rupees in the ratio 4 : 6 : 15 : 20 gives English 60, Urdu 90, Science 225 and Mathematics 300 rupees.

mcqs.q: If A : B = 2 : 5 and B : C = 5 : 4, then A : B : C = ?
mcqs.why:
The number for B is 5 in both ratios, so it stays the same.
We can join the ratios directly without changing anything.
So A : B : C = 2 : 5 : 4.

mcqs.q: If A : B = 3 : 7 and B : C = 8 : 9, then A : B : C = ?
mcqs.why:
Make B the same: 3 : 7 = 24 : 56 and 8 : 9 = 56 : 63.
Now B = 56 in both ratios.
So A : B : C = 24 : 56 : 63.

mcqs.q: If X : Y = 3 : 5 and X : Z = 4 : 9, then X : Y : Z = ?
mcqs.why:
Make X the same: 3 : 5 = 12 : 20 and 4 : 9 = 12 : 27.
Now X = 12 in both ratios.
So X : Y : Z = 12 : 20 : 27.

mcqs.q: Find x if x : 2 = 5 : 6.
mcqs.why:
From the proportion, cross-multiply: 6 × x = 2 × 5.
So 6x = 10.
Therefore x = 10/6 = 5/3.

mcqs.q: Find x if 4 : 5 = x : 7.
mcqs.why:
From the proportion, cross-multiply: 5 × x = 4 × 7.
So 5x = 28.
Therefore x = 28/5.

mcqs.q: Shazia : Nazia = 5 : 9 and Nazia : Madiha = 8 : 11. Their continued ratio is:
mcqs.why:
Make Nazia the same: 5 : 9 = 40 : 72 and 8 : 11 = 72 : 99.
Now Nazia = 72 in both ratios.
So Shazia : Nazia : Madiha = 40 : 72 : 99.

mcqs.q: 2000 rupees divided in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 gives Saleem (2 parts):
mcqs.why:
Sum of ratio terms = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10, so one share = 2000 / 10 = 200 rupees.
Saleem has 2 parts: 2 × 200 = 400 rupees.
Irfan gets 600 and Imran gets 1000 rupees.

mcqs.q: Akhtar : Aziz = 3 : 4 and Aziz : Anas = 5 : 7. Their continued ratio of marks is:
mcqs.why:
Make Aziz the same: 3 : 4 = 15 : 20 and 5 : 7 = 20 : 28.
Now Aziz = 20 in both ratios.
So Akhtar : Aziz : Anas = 15 : 20 : 28.

mcqs.q: 27,400 rupees is shared as Gas : Water : Electricity : Phone = 70 : 28 : 21 : 18. The gas bill is:
mcqs.why:
Sum of ratio terms = 137, so one share = 27400 / 137 = 200 rupees.
Gas has 70 parts: 70 × 200 = 14,000 rupees.
Water is 5,600, electricity 4,200 and phone 3,600 rupees.

mcqs.q: Books costing 675 rupees in total are in the ratio English : Urdu : Science : Mathematics = 4 : 6 : 15 : 20. The Mathematics book costs:
mcqs.why:
Sum of ratio terms = 45, so one share = 675 / 45 = 15 rupees.
Mathematics has 20 parts: 20 × 15 = 300 rupees.
English is 60, Urdu 90 and Science 225 rupees.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2 — Unitary and Proportion Methods
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

This exercise solves everyday problems in two ways. The unitary method first finds the value for ONE, then multiplies. The proportion method writes a proportion and cross-multiplies.

First decide: is it direct proportion (both grow together, like more chairs = more price) or inverse proportion (one grows, the other shrinks, like more taps = less time)?

Formula / Rule

Unitary method: value of 1 = total value ÷ total quantity, then value needed = value of 1 × quantity needed

Direct proportion: a : b = c : x. Inverse proportion: the total work stays the same, e.g. men × days stays constant

Worked Example

Question: The price of 15 chairs is 4,500 rupees. Find the price of 20 chairs.

Step 1 (unitary): Price of 1 chair = 4500 / 15 = 300 rupees.

Step 2: Price of 20 chairs = 20 × 300 = 6,000 rupees.

Step 3 (proportion check): 15 : 20 = 4500 : x, so 15x = 90,000 and x = 6,000 rupees.

Answer: 6,000 rupees.

Other Question Types in This Exercise

  • Direct: 4 kg mangoes for 300 rupees → 10 kg for 750 rupees. 6 kg spinach for 105 rupees → 18 kg for 315 rupees. Party for 35 guests costs 5,250 rupees → 85 guests cost 12,750 rupees.
  • Direct with fractions: 4/7 part of metal weighs 28 kg, so the whole is 49 kg and the 8/9 part weighs 392/9 = 43 5/9 kg.
  • Inverse: 6 taps fill a tank in 3 hours → 9 taps fill it in 2 hours. 5 men finish supplies in 8 days → 10 men finish in 4 days. 20 soldiers finish supplies in 8 days → 32 soldiers finish in 5 days.
  • Inverse for time: 4 labourers do a job in 8 hours → 6 labourers take 32/6 = 16/3 = 5 1/3 hours.

Remember

  • In inverse proportion, first find the total: e.g. 1 tap needs 6 × 3 = 18 hours, then divide by the new time.
  • Both methods must give the same answer — use one to check the other.
  • Reading example: 30 pages in 4 days means 7.5 pages per day, so 75 pages in 10 days.

mcqs.q: The price of 15 chairs is 4,500 rupees. The price of 20 chairs is:
mcqs.why:
Unitary method: price of 1 chair = 4500 / 15 = 300 rupees.
Price of 20 chairs = 20 × 300 = 6,000 rupees.
This is direct proportion: more chairs, more price.

mcqs.q: Six identical taps fill a tank in 3 hours. How many taps fill it in 2 hours?
mcqs.why:
This is inverse proportion: less time needs more taps.
1 tap would take 6 × 3 = 18 hours, so taps needed = 18 / 2 = 9.
Answer: 9 taps.

mcqs.q: 5 men finish a stock of supplies in 8 days. How many men finish it in 4 days?
mcqs.why:
This is inverse proportion: fewer days need more men.
1 man would take 5 × 8 = 40 days, so men needed = 40 / 4 = 10.
Answer: 10 men.

mcqs.q: The price of 4 kg of mangoes is 300 rupees. The price of 10 kg is:
mcqs.why:
Unitary method: price of 1 kg = 300 / 4 = 75 rupees.
Price of 10 kg = 10 × 75 = 750 rupees.
This is direct proportion.

mcqs.q: A student reads 30 pages in 4 days. In 10 days he will read:
mcqs.why:
In 1 day he reads 30 / 4 = 7.5 pages.
In 10 days he reads 10 × 7.5 = 75 pages.
This is direct proportion.

mcqs.q: 20 soldiers finish supplies in 8 days. How many soldiers finish the same supplies in 5 days?
mcqs.why:
This is inverse proportion.
1 soldier would take 20 × 8 = 160 days, so soldiers needed = 160 / 5 = 32.
Answer: 32 soldiers.

mcqs.q: 4 labourers complete a job in 8 hours. 6 labourers will take:
mcqs.why:
This is inverse proportion: more labourers, less time.
1 labourer would take 4 × 8 = 32 hours, so 6 labourers take 32 / 6 = 16/3 hours.
That is 5 hours and 20 minutes.

mcqs.q: The price of 6 kg of spinach is 105 rupees. The price of 18 kg is:
mcqs.why:
Price of 1 kg = 105 / 6 = 17.5 rupees.
Price of 18 kg = 18 × 17.5 = 315 rupees.
18 kg is exactly 3 times 6 kg, and 3 × 105 = 315.

mcqs.q: The weight of the 4/7 part of a piece of metal is 28 kg. The weight of the 8/9 part is:
mcqs.why:
Whole weight = 28 × 7/4 = 49 kg.
Weight of 8/9 part = 49 × 8/9 = 392/9 kg.
That is 43 5/9 kg.

mcqs.q: A party of 35 guests costs 5,250 rupees. A party of 85 guests costs:
mcqs.why:
Cost per guest = 5250 / 35 = 150 rupees.
Cost for 85 guests = 85 × 150 = 12,750 rupees.
This is direct proportion.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3 — Direct and Inverse Proportion at Work
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

Here we use direct and inverse proportion with labourers, work and fodder — without writing full proportions every time. The key is the total work.

In inverse proportion, workers × time stays the same (labourer-days). In direct proportion, more workers in the same time means more work done.

Formula / Rule

Inverse proportion: number of workers × time = total work (constant). New workers = total work ÷ new time; new time = total work ÷ new workers

Direct proportion: work done grows in the same ratio as the workers (for the same time)

Worked Example

Question: 12 labourers build a bungalow in 64 days. How many days will 18 labourers take?

Step 1: This is inverse proportion — more labourers means fewer days.

Step 2: Total work = 12 × 64 = 768 labourer-days.

Step 3: Days for 18 labourers = 768 / 18 = 128/3 = 42 2/3 days.

Answer: 42 2/3 days (42 days and 16 hours).

Other Question Types in This Exercise

  • Direct, less work: 20 labourers complete half a job in a given time, so a quarter of the job in the same time needs 20 × 1/2 = 10 labourers.
  • Inverse, more days: 6 labourers in 10 days → 60/15 = 4 labourers in 15 days. 5 labourers in 8 days → 40/4 = 10 labourers in 4 days.
  • Inverse, find days: 3 weavers weave cloth in 4 days → 5 weavers take 12/5 = 2 2/5 days.
  • Direct, more work: 5 men complete 1/3 of a job, so 1 man does 1/15 and 7 men do 7/15 of the job in the same time.
  • Fodder: 1500 sheep × 75 days = 112,500 sheep-days, so the fodder lasts 1250 sheep for 90 days, and 1200 sheep for 93.75 days.

Remember

  • Ask first: if workers increase, does time increase (direct with work) or decrease (inverse)?
  • Always calculate the total (workers × days) first in inverse questions.
  • Fractions of work scale directly: half the work needs half the workers in the same time.

mcqs.q: 20 labourers complete half of a job in a certain time. How many labourers complete a quarter of the job in the same time?
mcqs.why:
This is direct proportion: less work needs fewer labourers.
A quarter is half of a half, so workers are also halved.
20 × (1/4) / (1/2) = 10 labourers.

mcqs.q: 6 labourers complete a job in 10 days. How many labourers are needed in 15 days?
mcqs.why:
This is inverse proportion: total work = 6 × 10 = 60 labourer-days.
Labourers needed = 60 / 15 = 4.
More days means fewer labourers.

mcqs.q: 5 labourers complete a job in 8 days. How many labourers are needed in 4 days?
mcqs.why:
Total work = 5 × 8 = 40 labourer-days.
Labourers needed = 40 / 4 = 10.
Halving the days doubles the labourers — inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: 3 weavers weave a cloth in 4 days. 5 weavers will take:
mcqs.why:
Total work = 3 × 4 = 12 weaver-days.
Days for 5 weavers = 12 / 5 = 2 2/5 days.
More weavers means fewer days — inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: 5 men complete 1/3 part of a job in some time. In the same time, 7 men will complete:
mcqs.why:
This is direct proportion: 1 man completes (1/3) / 5 = 1/15 part.
7 men complete 7 × 1/15 = 7/15 part.
More men means more work in the same time.

mcqs.q: 12 labourers build a bungalow in 64 days. 18 labourers will take:
mcqs.why:
Total work = 12 × 64 = 768 labourer-days.
Days for 18 labourers = 768 / 18 = 128/3 = 42 2/3 days.
That is 42 days and 16 hours.

mcqs.q: Fodder for 1500 sheep lasts 75 days. How many sheep will finish it in 90 days?
mcqs.why:
Total = 1500 × 75 = 112,500 sheep-days.
Sheep for 90 days = 112500 / 90 = 1250.
More days means fewer sheep — inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: The same fodder for 1500 sheep lasting 75 days will last 1200 sheep for:
mcqs.why:
Total = 1500 × 75 = 112,500 sheep-days.
Days for 1200 sheep = 112500 / 1200 = 93.75 days.
That is 93 days and 18 hours.

mcqs.q: In the question '6 labourers complete a job in 10 days', what is the total work?
mcqs.why:
Total work = labourers × days = 6 × 10.
That gives 60 labourer-days.
This total stays the same when the number of days changes in inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: Why is 'more labourers, fewer days for the same job' inverse proportion?
options: Because workers × days (total work) stays the same
Because the days increase with labourers
mcqs.why:
For the same job, the total work does not change.
If workers go up, days must go down so workers × days stays constant.
That constant product is the sign of inverse proportion in this unit.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4 — Speed, Distance and Time
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

Speed tells us how much distance is covered in one unit of time. This exercise converts speed between kilometres per hour (km/h) and metres per second (m/s), and finds speed, distance and time.

Formula / Rule

Speed = distance ÷ time; Distance = speed × time; Time = distance ÷ speed

To change km/h into m/s: multiply by 1000/3600 (which is 5/18)

To change m/s into km/h: multiply by 3600/1000 (which is 18/5)

Worked Example

Question: A car covers 210 kilometres in 3 hours. Find its speed per hour, and the distance it covers in 4 1/2 hours.

Step 1: Speed = distance / time = 210 / 3 = 70 kilometres per hour.

Step 2: Distance = speed × time = 70 × 4 1/2 = 70 × 9/2.

Step 3: 70 × 9/2 = 315 kilometres.

Answers: speed 70 km/h; distance in 4 1/2 hours is 315 kilometres. It would take 350 / 70 = 5 hours to cover 350 kilometres.

Other Question Types in This Exercise

  • km/h to m/s: 50 km/h = 125/9 = 13 8/9 m/s, 75 km/h = 125/6 = 20 5/6 m/s, 80 km/h = 200/9 = 22 2/9 m/s.
  • m/s to km/h: 30 m/s = 108 km/h, 12 m/s = 43.2 km/h, 42 m/s = 151.2 km/h, 25.5 m/s = 91.8 km/h.
  • Speed: a motorcycle covering 80 km in 2 hours has speed 40 km/h.
  • Time: a van at 60 km/h takes 180 / 60 = 3 hours for 180 km. A bus going 60 km/h for 3 hours covers 180 km, so at 70 km/h it takes 180/70 = 18/7 = 2 4/7 hours.
  • Small units: a cyclist covering 150 m in 30 s has speed 5 m/s, so in 45 s he covers 225 m. 70 km/h = 7/6 km per minute.

Remember

  • Always write the unit with the answer: km/h, m/s or km per minute.
  • 1 kilometre = 1000 metres and 1 hour = 3600 seconds — that is where 1000/3600 comes from.
  • Check which formula you need: speed, distance or time — you are always given the other two.

mcqs.q: 50 kilometres per hour in metres per second is:
mcqs.why:
Multiply by 1000/3600: 50 × 1000/3600 = 500/36.
Simplify to 125/9.
That is 13 8/9 m/s, about 13.89 m/s.

mcqs.q: 80 kilometres per hour in metres per second is:
mcqs.why:
Multiply by 1000/3600: 80 × 1000/3600 = 800/36.
Simplify to 200/9.
That is 22 2/9 m/s, about 22.22 m/s.

mcqs.q: 30 metres per second in kilometres per hour is:
mcqs.why:
Multiply by 3600/1000: 30 × 3600/1000.
That equals 108.
So 30 m/s = 108 km/h.

mcqs.q: 25.5 metres per second in kilometres per hour is:
A motorcycle covers 80 kilometres in 2 hours. Its speed is:
mcqs.why:
Speed = distance / time.
Speed = 80 / 2 = 40.
So the speed is 40 kilometres per hour.

mcqs.q: A van at 60 km/h covers 180 kilometres in:
mcqs.why:
Time = distance / speed.
Time = 180 / 60 = 3.
So the van takes 3 hours.

mcqs.q: A cyclist covers 150 metres in 30 seconds. In 45 seconds he will cover:
mcqs.why:
Speed = 150 / 30 = 5 metres per second.
Distance in 45 seconds = 5 × 45 = 225 metres.
Use distance = speed × time.

mcqs.q: A car covers 210 km in 3 hours. Its speed in metres per second is:
mcqs.why:
First speed = 210 / 3 = 70 km/h.
Convert: 70 × 1000/3600 = 175/9.
That is 19 4/9 m/s, about 19.44 m/s.

mcqs.q: At 70 km/h, the distance covered in 4 1/2 hours is:
mcqs.why:
Distance = speed × time = 70 × 4 1/2.
70 × 9/2 = 630/2 = 315.
So the car covers 315 kilometres.

mcqs.q: A bus travels at 60 km/h for 3 hours. At 70 km/h, the same distance takes:
mcqs.why:
Distance = 60 × 3 = 180 kilometres.
New time = 180 / 70 = 18/7 = 2 4/7 hours.
Faster speed means less time for the same distance.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 6 — Proportion: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

This review mixes all of Unit 6: continued ratios, finding x in a proportion, sharing in a ratio, direct and inverse proportion problems, speed conversions, and speed-distance-time questions.

Formula / Rule

Make the common term equal to join ratios; one share = total ÷ sum of ratio terms

In a proportion, cross-multiply to find the unknown, e.g. x : 5 = 6 : 15 gives 15x = 30

Inverse proportion: workers × days stays constant. Speed = distance ÷ time; km/h to m/s multiply by 1000/3600, m/s to km/h multiply by 3600/1000

Worked Example

Question: A car covers 30 kilometres in 25 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 55 minutes, and what is its speed?

Step 1: Distance in 55 minutes = 30/25 × 55 = 66 kilometres.

Step 2: Speed in km/h = 30 × 60/25 = 72 kilometres per hour.

Step 3: Speed in km per minute = 30/25 = 1.2 kilometres per minute.

Step 4: Speed in m/s = 72 × 1000/3600 = 20 metres per second.

Other Question Types in This Exercise

  • Continued ratio: x : y = 2 : 5 and x : z = 4 : 7 gives x : y : z = 4 : 10 : 7. P : Q : R : S = 105 : 140 : 168 : 192.
  • Direct: 10 pens cost 250 rupees, so 1 pen costs 25 rupees and 17 pens cost 425 rupees. Carrying goods 40 km costs 100 rupees, so 150 km costs 375 rupees and 560 rupees carries goods 224 km.
  • Inverse: 10 labourers finish a job in 7 days (70 labourer-days), so in 5 days 70/5 = 14 labourers are needed.
  • Sharing: petrol in the ratio 7 : 9 : 11 with total 162 litres gives 42, 54 and 66 litres, because one share = 162/27 = 6 litres.
  • Conversions: 60 km/h = 50/3 = 16 2/3 m/s, and 105 m/s = 378 km/h.

Remember

  • For 7 : 8 = y : 24, cross-multiply: 8y = 168, so y = 21.
  • Always check sharing answers add to the total: 42 + 54 + 66 = 162.
  • Minutes must be changed carefully: 25 minutes is used with × 60 to get speed per hour.

mcqs.q: If x : y = 2 : 5 and x : z = 4 : 7, then x : y : z = ?
mcqs.why:
Make x the same: 2 : 5 = 4 : 10, and x : z is already 4 : 7.
Now x = 4 in both ratios.
So x : y : z = 4 : 10 : 7.

mcqs.q: The price of 10 pens is 250 rupees. The price of 17 pens is:
mcqs.why:
Price of 1 pen = 250 / 10 = 25 rupees.
Price of 17 pens = 17 × 25 = 425 rupees.
This is direct proportion.

mcqs.q: 10 labourers complete a job in 7 days. How many labourers are needed in 5 days?
mcqs.why:
This is inverse proportion: total work = 10 × 7 = 70 labourer-days.
Labourers needed = 70 / 5 = 14.
Fewer days need more labourers.

mcqs.q: If x : 5 = 6 : 15, then x = ?
mcqs.why:
Cross-multiply: 15 × x = 5 × 6.
So 15x = 30.
Therefore x = 30/15 = 2.

mcqs.q: If 7 : 8 = y : 24, then y = ?
mcqs.why:
Cross-multiply: 8 × y = 7 × 24.
So 8y = 168.
Therefore y = 168/8 = 21.

mcqs.q: 60 kilometres per hour in metres per second is:
mcqs.why:
Multiply by 1000/3600: 60 × 1000/3600 = 600/36.
Simplify to 50/3.
That is 16 2/3 m/s, about 16.67 m/s.

mcqs.q: 105 metres per second in kilometres per hour is:
Petrol for cars A, B, C is in the ratio 7 : 9 : 11, total 162 litres. Car C uses:
mcqs.why:
Sum of ratio terms = 27, so one share = 162 / 27 = 6 litres.
Car C has 11 parts: 11 × 6 = 66 litres.
Car A uses 42 and car B uses 54 litres.

mcqs.q: A car covers 30 km in 25 minutes. Its speed is:
mcqs.why:
Speed = 30 × 60/25 = 72 km/h, and in km per minute it is 30/25 = 1.2.
Convert 72 km/h: 72 × 1000/3600 = 20 m/s.
In 55 minutes it covers 66 km.

mcqs.q: Carrying goods up to 40 km costs 100 rupees. Carrying up to 150 km costs:
mcqs.why:
Cost per km = 100 / 40 rupees.
Cost for 150 km = 100/40 × 150 = 375 rupees.
Note: 224 km is the distance for 560 rupees, the other part of the question.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1 — Property Tax
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

A tax is the money the government collects from people's income, production or services so that the country's expenses can be met. Taxes pay for defence, police, education, health and other public services.

Property tax is the tax the government takes every year on a person's property or personal estate. Its rate is generally about 2% of the value of the property.

Some properties pay no tax: government properties, a residential building on 120 square yards of land or less, a building with a covered area of 600 square feet or less, and places like a library, garden, place of worship, orphanage and cemetery.

Formula / Rule

Property tax = Value of property × Rate ÷ 100

Value of property = Tax × 100 ÷ Rate

Rate = Tax ÷ Value of property × 100

Worked Example

Find the property tax on a property worth Rs. 286,400 at the rate of 5%.

Step 1: Write the formula: Property tax = Value × Rate ÷ 100.

Step 2: Put in the values: Tax = 286,400 × 5 ÷ 100.

Step 3: Multiply: 286,400 × 5 = 1,432,000.

Step 4: Divide by 100: 1,432,000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 14,320.

Remember

  • There are three kinds of questions: find the tax, find the value, or find the rate. Choose the right formula each time.
  • Tax of Rs. 25,500 at 2% means the property value is Rs. 1,275,000.
  • Tax of Rs. 33,000 on a property of Rs. 3,300,000 means the rate is 1%.

mcqs.q: What is the property tax on a property worth Rs. 286,400 at the rate of 5%?
mcqs.why: Property tax = 286,400 × 5 ÷ 100 = 1,432,000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 14,320. Always multiply the value by the rate and then divide by 100 to find a percentage tax.

mcqs.q: The value of a property is Rs. 814,500 and the tax rate is 3%. What is the property tax?
mcqs.why: Property tax = 814,500 × 3 ÷ 100 = 2,443,500 ÷ 100 = Rs. 24,435. This uses the same formula: value × rate ÷ 100.

mcqs.q: Property tax of Rs. 4,800 was paid at the rate of 5%. What was the value of the property?
mcqs.why: Value = Tax × 100 ÷ Rate = 4,800 × 100 ÷ 5 = 480,000 ÷ 5 = Rs. 96,000. When the tax and rate are given, work backwards with this formula.

mcqs.q: Property tax of Rs. 11,700 was paid at the rate of 1.5%. What was the value of the property?
mcqs.why: Value = 11,700 × 100 ÷ 1.5 = 1,170,000 ÷ 1.5 = Rs. 780,000. Divide carefully when the rate has a decimal point.

mcqs.q: Property tax of Rs. 12,000 was paid on a property worth Rs. 600,000. What is the tax rate?
mcqs.why: Rate = Tax ÷ Value × 100 = 12,000 ÷ 600,000 × 100 = 2%. The rate tells what percent of the value was paid as tax.

mcqs.q: Property tax of Rs. 33,000 was paid on a property worth Rs. 3,300,000. What is the tax rate?
mcqs.why: Rate = 33,000 ÷ 3,300,000 × 100 = 1%. Here the tax is a very small part of the value, so the rate is small too.

mcqs.q: What is a tax?
options: Money a shopkeeper keeps as profit
Money paid only by rich people
Money the government collects to meet the country's expenses
Money a bank lends to people
mcqs.why: A tax is the amount the government collects from people's income, production or services. It is used so that the country's expenses, like defence and education, can be met.

mcqs.q: Which of these properties is exempt from property tax?
options: A big shop in a market
mcqs.why: Places of worship are exempt from tax, along with government properties, libraries, gardens, orphanages and cemeteries. Small homes on 120 square yards or less are also exempt.

mcqs.q: The value of a property is Rs. 234,000 and the tax rate is 1.4%. What is the property tax?
mcqs.why: Property tax = 234,000 × 1.4 ÷ 100 = 327,600 ÷ 100 = Rs. 3,276. A rate like 1.4% is used in the same way as a whole-number rate.

mcqs.q: Why does the government levy a tax?
options: To meet government expenses like defence, police, education and health
To increase the price of property
mcqs.why: The purpose of levying a tax is to meet the government's expenses. These include defence, police, education, health and other public services for everyone.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.2 — General Sales Tax (GST)
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

GST means General Sales Tax. It is a tax added to the price of goods when we buy them. In this exercise the GST rate is 17% for every question.

Sometimes you are given the price without tax and must find the GST. Sometimes you are given the total price, which already includes GST, and must find the price without GST.

Formula / Rule

GST = Price of item × 17% = Price × 0.17

Total price = Price of item + GST

Price without GST = Total price ÷ 1.17

GST rate = GST ÷ Price of item × 100

Worked Example

A microwave oven costs Rs. 15,200. Find the GST at 17% and the total price.

Step 1: GST = 15,200 × 0.17 = Rs. 2,584.

Step 2: Total price = Price + GST.

Step 3: Total price = 15,200 + 2,584 = Rs. 17,784.

Remember

  • If the total price includes GST, divide by 1.17 to remove the GST. Example: Rs. 35,375 ÷ 1.17 = Rs. 30,235.04.
  • If you know the GST and the rate, Price = GST ÷ 0.17. Example: Rs. 2,720 ÷ 0.17 = Rs. 16,000.
  • GST = Total price − Price of item. Example: 14,976 − 12,800 = Rs. 2,176.

mcqs.q: A Parker pen costs Rs. 875. What is the GST on it at the rate of 17%?
mcqs.why: GST = 875 × 0.17 = Rs. 148.75. To find 17% of a price, multiply the price by 0.17.

mcqs.q: A mobile phone costs Rs. 4,850. What is the GST at the rate of 17%?
mcqs.why: GST = 4,850 × 0.17 = Rs. 824.50. The GST is only the tax part, not the total price including the phone.

mcqs.q: The total price of cosmetics is Rs. 14,976 and the actual price is Rs. 12,800. What is the GST?
mcqs.why: GST = Total price − Actual price = 14,976 − 12,800 = Rs. 2,176. Check: 12,800 × 17% = 2,176, so the answer is correct.

mcqs.q: A microwave oven costs Rs. 15,200 with GST at 17%. What is the total price?
mcqs.why: GST = 15,200 × 0.17 = Rs. 2,584, so total price = 15,200 + 2,584 = Rs. 17,784. Total price always means price plus GST.

mcqs.q: A refrigerator was sold for Rs. 35,375 including 17% GST. What is its actual price?
mcqs.why: Actual price = Total price ÷ 1.17 = 35,375 ÷ 1.17 = Rs. 30,235.04 approximately. Divide by 1.17 whenever the given price already includes 17% GST.

mcqs.q: Abdullah bought a watch for Rs. 7,880 including GST at 17%. About how much GST is in this price?
mcqs.why: Price without GST = 7,880 ÷ 1.17 = Rs. 6,735.04, so GST = 7,880 − 6,735.04 = Rs. 1,144.96, about Rs. 1,145. First remove the GST, then subtract.

mcqs.q: Alia paid Rs. 2,720 GST at the rate of 17%. What was the price of the items without GST?
mcqs.why: Price = GST ÷ Rate = 2,720 ÷ 0.17 = Rs. 16,000. If 17% of the price is Rs. 2,720, dividing by 0.17 gives the full price.

mcqs.q: An electric company charges Rs. 1,547 GST on electricity usage of Rs. 9,100. What is the GST rate?
mcqs.why: GST rate = GST ÷ Price × 100 = 1,547 ÷ 9,100 × 100 = 17%. This is the standard GST rate used in this whole exercise.

mcqs.q: A person bought a dishwasher for Rs. 61,000 including GST. About how much is the GST?
mcqs.why: Price without GST = 61,000 ÷ 1.17 = Rs. 52,136.75, so GST = 61,000 − 52,136.75 = Rs. 8,863.25 approximately. The GST is the difference between the two prices.

mcqs.q: The price of a shirt without tax is Rs. 2,560 and the GST on it is Rs. 436. What is the rate of GST?
mcqs.why: Rate = 436 ÷ 2,560 × 100 = 17.03%, which is about 17%. Small rounding in the GST amount makes the rate come out just above 17%.

lessons.title: Practical Work — Profit, Profit Rate and Mark-up Tables
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

This practical work fills in missing values in tables. You use one formula at a time. Cost price is what a thing is bought for. Selling price is what it is sold for. If the selling price is more, there is a profit.

Mark-up here is the extra amount charged on a principal for a given rate and time, like interest on a loan.

Formula / Rule

Profit = Selling price − Cost price

Selling price = Cost price + Profit

Cost price = Selling price − Profit

Profit rate (in these tables) = Profit ÷ Selling price × 100

Mark-up = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100

Worked Example

Principal is Rs. 500, the period is 2 years and the mark-up rate is 12%. Find the mark-up.

Step 1: Write the formula: Mark-up = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100.

Step 2: Put in the values: Mark-up = 500 × 12 × 2 ÷ 100.

Step 3: Multiply: 500 × 12 × 2 = 12,000.

Step 4: Divide by 100: 12,000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 120.

Remember

  • Principal = Mark-up × 100 ÷ (Rate × Time). Example: 205 × 100 ÷ (8 × 1) = Rs. 2,562.50.
  • Rate = Mark-up × 100 ÷ (Principal × Time). Example: 528 × 100 ÷ (1,650 × 10) = 3.2%.
  • Time = Mark-up × 100 ÷ (Principal × Rate). Example: 350 × 100 ÷ (3,500 × 2.5) = 4 years.

mcqs.q: Cost price is Rs. 1,600 and selling price is Rs. 1,750. What is the profit?
mcqs.why: Profit = Selling price − Cost price = 1,750 − 1,600 = Rs. 150. Profit is how much more you sold for than you bought for.

mcqs.q: Cost price is Rs. 2,000 and profit is Rs. 600. What is the selling price?
mcqs.why: Selling price = Cost price + Profit = 2,000 + 600 = Rs. 2,600. Add the profit to the cost price to get the selling price.

mcqs.q: Selling price is Rs. 10,450 and profit is Rs. 950. What is the cost price?
mcqs.why: Cost price = Selling price − Profit = 10,450 − 950 = Rs. 9,500. Take the profit away from the selling price.

mcqs.q: Selling price is Rs. 1,000, cost price is Rs. 800 and profit is Rs. 200. Using Profit rate = Profit ÷ Selling price × 100, what is the profit rate?
mcqs.why: Profit rate = 200 ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 20%. In these tables the profit rate is found on the selling price, as the formula in the table says.

mcqs.q: Cost price is Rs. 1,000 and the profit rate is 10%. Using Selling price = Cost price × (1 + Profit rate), what is the selling price?
mcqs.why: Selling price = 1,000 × (1 + 0.10) = 1,000 × 1.10 = Rs. 1,100. Change 10% to 0.10 before using this formula.

mcqs.q: Principal is Rs. 500, rate is 12% and time is 2 years. What is the mark-up?
mcqs.why: Mark-up = 500 × 12 × 2 ÷ 100 = 12,000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 120. Multiply principal, rate and time together, then divide by 100.

mcqs.q: Mark-up is Rs. 205, rate is 8% and time is 1 year. What is the principal?
mcqs.why: Principal = Mark-up × 100 ÷ (Rate × Time) = 205 × 100 ÷ (8 × 1) = 20,500 ÷ 8 = Rs. 2,562.50. This is the mark-up formula turned around.

mcqs.q: Principal is Rs. 1,650, mark-up is Rs. 528 and time is 10 years. What is the rate?
mcqs.why: Rate = Mark-up × 100 ÷ (Principal × Time) = 528 × 100 ÷ (1,650 × 10) = 52,800 ÷ 16,500 = 3.2%. Use this form when the rate is the missing value.

mcqs.q: Principal is Rs. 3,500, mark-up is Rs. 350 and rate is 2.5%. What is the time?
mcqs.why: Time = Mark-up × 100 ÷ (Principal × Rate) = 350 × 100 ÷ (3,500 × 2.5) = 35,000 ÷ 8,750 = 4 years. The answer for time comes out in years.

mcqs.q: Principal is Rs. 100,000, rate is 1.25% and time is 3 years. What is the mark-up?
mcqs.why: Mark-up = 100,000 × 1.25 × 3 ÷ 100 = 375,000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 3,750. Even a small rate like 1.25% is used in exactly the same formula.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.3 — Profit and Mark-up Rate
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

A shopkeeper buys at the cost price and sells at a higher selling price. The extra money is the profit. The profit rate in this exercise is found on the cost price.

Many shops fix a mark-up rate. The selling price is then the cost price plus that percent of the cost price.

For a whole business, total profit = income − cost of goods − other expenses, and profit percentage = total profit ÷ total sales × 100.

Formula / Rule

Profit = Selling price − Cost price

Profit rate = Profit ÷ Cost price × 100

Selling price = Cost price × (1 + Rate)

Cost price = Selling price ÷ (1 + Rate)

Worked Example

A shopkeeper bought a helmet for Rs. 1,860 and sold it for Rs. 2,650. Find the profit and profit rate.

Step 1: Profit = 2,650 − 1,860 = Rs. 790.

Step 2: Profit rate = Profit ÷ Cost price × 100.

Step 3: Profit rate = 790 ÷ 1,860 × 100 = 42.47% approximately.

Remember

  • With a 65% mark-up on an item costing Rs. 1,520, selling price = 1,520 × 1.65 = Rs. 2,508.
  • To go back from selling price to cost price, divide by (1 + Rate). Example: 1,230 ÷ 1.5 = Rs. 820 at a 50% mark-up.
  • Returned goods are taken away from sales before finding business profit.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper bought a helmet for Rs. 1,860 and sold it for Rs. 2,650. What is the profit?
mcqs.why: Profit = 2,650 − 1,860 = Rs. 790. The profit rate on this is 790 ÷ 1,860 × 100 = 42.47% approximately.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper bought a microwave oven for Rs. 6,250 and sold it for Rs. 6,700. What is the profit rate on the cost price?
mcqs.why: Profit = 6,700 − 6,250 = Rs. 450, and profit rate = 450 ÷ 6,250 × 100 = 7.2%. In this exercise the profit rate is always on the cost price.

mcqs.q: The cost price of an item is Rs. 1,520 and the mark-up rate is 65%. What is the selling price?
mcqs.why: Selling price = 1,520 × (1 + 0.65) = 1,520 × 1.65 = Rs. 2,508. Add 1 to the rate in decimal form, then multiply by the cost price.

mcqs.q: The cost price of a novel is Rs. 1,100. What is its selling price at a 66% mark-up rate?
mcqs.why: Selling price = 1,100 × (1 + 0.66) = 1,100 × 1.66 = Rs. 1,826. A 66% mark-up means the selling price is 166% of the cost price.

mcqs.q: The cost price of a mobile is Rs. 2,260 and the mark-up rate is 55%. What is the selling price?
mcqs.why: Selling price = 2,260 × (1 + 0.55) = 2,260 × 1.55 = Rs. 3,503. Multiply the cost price by 1.55 for a 55% mark-up.

mcqs.q: A mobile is sold for Rs. 4,785 at a 45% mark-up rate. What is its cost price?
mcqs.why: Cost price = Selling price ÷ (1 + Rate) = 4,785 ÷ 1.45 = Rs. 3,300. Divide, do not multiply, when you go back from selling price to cost price.

mcqs.q: The selling price of a calculator is Rs. 1,230 and the mark-up rate is 50%. What is the cost price?
mcqs.why: Cost price = 1,230 ÷ (1 + 0.50) = 1,230 ÷ 1.5 = Rs. 820. At 50% mark-up the selling price is one and a half times the cost price.

mcqs.q: An item is sold for Rs. 144 at a 60% mark-up. What is its cost price?
mcqs.why: Cost price = 144 ÷ (1 + 0.60) = 144 ÷ 1.6 = Rs. 90. Check: 90 × 1.6 = 144, so the answer is right.

mcqs.q: A home business has monthly income Rs. 25,000 and total costs Rs. 10,550. What is the profit percentage on total sales?
mcqs.why: Total profit = 25,000 − 10,550 = Rs. 14,450, and profit percentage = 14,450 ÷ 25,000 × 100 = 57.8%. First find the profit in rupees, then turn it into a percent of sales.

mcqs.q: Monthly earnings are Rs. 1,850,000, returned goods are Rs. 85,000, cost of goods is Rs. 850,000 and administrative expenses are Rs. 550,000. What is the profit percentage?
mcqs.why: Net sales = 1,850,000 − 85,000 = Rs. 1,765,000. Total profit = 1,765,000 − 850,000 − 550,000 = Rs. 365,000, and 365,000 ÷ 1,765,000 × 100 = 20.68% approximately. Returned goods must be subtracted first.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.4 — Mark-up, Zakat and Ushr
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

This exercise has two parts. First, bank mark-up: extra money charged on a principal for a rate and a time. Time given in months is changed to years by dividing by 12, and time in days by dividing by 365.

Second, Zakat and Ushr. Zakat is 2.5% of savings and valuables kept for a whole year by a person who is sahib-e-nisab (whose wealth is above the nisab limit). Ushr is paid on farm produce; in this exercise the rate is 5%.

Formula / Rule

Mark-up = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100

Selling price (with loan) = Principal + Mark-up

Zakat = Total amount × 2.5% = Total amount × 0.025

Ushr = Value of produce × 5% = Value × 0.05

Worked Example

Qasim bought a car for Rs. 450,800 with a bank loan at 12% mark-up for 3 years. Find the selling price.

Step 1: Mark-up = 450,800 × 12 × 3 ÷ 100 = Rs. 162,288.

Step 2: Selling price = Principal + Mark-up.

Step 3: Selling price = 450,800 + 162,288 = Rs. 613,088.

Remember

  • 9 months = 9 ÷ 12 = 0.75 years; 219 days = 219 ÷ 365 = 0.6 years.
  • For Zakat, first add cash and the value of gold or goods, then take 2.5%. Example: (200,000 + 3 × 47,400) × 2.5% = Rs. 8,555.
  • To find savings from Zakat paid, divide by 0.025. Example: 20,500 ÷ 0.025 = Rs. 820,000.

mcqs.q: Qasim bought a car for Rs. 450,800 at 12% annual mark-up for 3 years. What is the mark-up?
mcqs.why: Mark-up = 450,800 × 12 × 3 ÷ 100 = Rs. 162,288. The selling price of the car then becomes 450,800 + 162,288 = Rs. 613,088.

mcqs.q: Najma bought a jewellery set for Rs. 175,500 at 10% mark-up for 9 months. What is the selling price?
mcqs.why: Time = 9 ÷ 12 = 0.75 years. Mark-up = 175,500 × 10 × 0.75 ÷ 100 = Rs. 13,162.50, so selling price = 175,500 + 13,162.50 = Rs. 188,662.50. Always change months into years first.

mcqs.q: The mark-up on a TV is Rs. 8,500 for 1½ years at 15%. What is the purchase price?
mcqs.why: Principal = Mark-up × 100 ÷ (Rate × Time) = 8,500 × 100 ÷ (15 × 1.5) = 850,000 ÷ 22.5 = Rs. 37,777.78 approximately. Use the turned-around mark-up formula.

mcqs.q: Principal is Rs. 800,000, rate is 12% and time is 1 year. What is the mark-up?
mcqs.why: Mark-up = 800,000 × 12 × 1 ÷ 100 = Rs. 96,000. For 1 year the mark-up is simply 12% of the principal.

mcqs.q: Mark-up is Rs. 6,600, rate is 11% and time is 2 years. What is the principal?
mcqs.why: Principal = 6,600 × 100 ÷ (11 × 2) = 660,000 ÷ 22 = Rs. 30,000. Multiply rate by time in the bottom part of the formula.

mcqs.q: A person keeps Rs. 50,000 for a whole year and it is above the nisab. How much Zakat does he pay?
mcqs.why: Zakat = 50,000 × 2.5% = 50,000 × 0.025 = Rs. 1,250. Zakat is always 2.5% of the total amount kept for a full year.

mcqs.q: A lady doctor has jewellery worth Rs. 500,000 and savings of Rs. 150,000. How much Zakat does she pay?
mcqs.why: Total amount = 500,000 + 150,000 = Rs. 650,000. Zakat = 650,000 × 2.5% = Rs. 16,250. Add all the wealth first, then take 2.5%.

mcqs.q: A trader paid Rs. 20,500 as Zakat. What were his savings for the whole year?
mcqs.why: Savings = Zakat ÷ 2.5% = 20,500 ÷ 0.025 = Rs. 820,000. Divide by 0.025 to work back from Zakat to the full amount.

mcqs.q: A farmer produces 15,000 kg of wheat at Rs. 5.25 per kg. What is the Ushr at 5%?
mcqs.why: Value of wheat = 15,000 × 5.25 = Rs. 78,750. Ushr = 78,750 × 5% = Rs. 3,937.50. First find the value of the produce, then take 5%.

mcqs.q: Juman sold the orange produce of his orchard for Rs. 5,000,000. What is the Ushr at 5%?
mcqs.why: Ushr = 5,000,000 × 5% = 5,000,000 × 0.05 = Rs. 250,000. Ushr in this exercise is 5% of the value of the produce.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 7 — Financial Arithmetic: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

This review mixes all of Unit 7: GST at 17%, bank mark-up, the shop mark-up rate, Zakat at 2.5% and Ushr at 5%. Read each question carefully and pick the right formula.

Formula / Rule

GST = Price × 0.17 and Price without GST = Total price ÷ 1.17

Mark-up = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100

Cost price = Selling price ÷ (1 + Mark-up rate)

Zakat = Total amount × 0.025 and Ushr = Value of produce × 0.05

Worked Example

A trader took a loan of Rs. 1,700,000 at 12.5% mark-up for 1½ years. Find the mark-up.

Step 1: Write the formula: Mark-up = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100.

Step 2: Put in the values: Mark-up = 1,700,000 × 12.5 × 1.5 ÷ 100.

Step 3: Multiply and divide: Mark-up = Rs. 318,750.

Remember

  • Price of a room set from GST alone: Price = GST ÷ 0.17. Example: 16,989 ÷ 0.17 = Rs. 99,935.29.
  • 6 months = 0.5 years. Principal from mark-up Rs. 2,850 at 12% for 6 months = 2,850 × 100 ÷ (12 × 0.5) = Rs. 47,500.
  • Amount from Zakat paid: Amount = Zakat ÷ 0.025. Example: 12,500 ÷ 0.025 = Rs. 500,000.

mcqs.q: The price of a mobile phone is Rs. 8,500 and GST is 17%. What is the selling price including GST?
mcqs.why: GST = 8,500 × 0.17 = Rs. 1,445, so selling price = 8,500 + 1,445 = Rs. 9,945. The tax charged on the sale is Rs. 1,445.

mcqs.q: An LCD TV is sold for Rs. 55,800 including 17% GST. About what is its price without tax?
mcqs.why: Price without tax = 55,800 ÷ 1.17 = Rs. 47,692.31 approximately. The GST in the price is then 55,800 − 47,692.31 = Rs. 8,107.69 approximately.

mcqs.q: An electric company charges Rs. 16,750 for electricity. What GST will the consumer pay at 17%?
mcqs.why: GST = 16,750 × 0.17 = Rs. 2,847.50. Multiply the bill amount by 0.17 to get the GST at 17%.

mcqs.q: At 12.5% mark-up, a loan of Rs. 1,700,000 for 1½ years gives what mark-up?
mcqs.why: Mark-up = 1,700,000 × 12.5 × 1.5 ÷ 100 = Rs. 318,750. Use principal, rate and time together in the mark-up formula.

mcqs.q: A lady doctor paid Rs. 2,850 mark-up for 6 months at 12%. What was the principal?
mcqs.why: Time = 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5 years. Principal = 2,850 × 100 ÷ (12 × 0.5) = 285,000 ÷ 6 = Rs. 47,500. Change 6 months to half a year first.

mcqs.q: Rs. 500,000 is deposited at 10% mark-up for 2½ years. What is the mark-up?
mcqs.why: Mark-up = 500,000 × 10 × 2.5 ÷ 100 = Rs. 125,000. The time 2½ years is written as 2.5 in the formula.

mcqs.q: A car is sold for Rs. 1,051,000 at a 35% mark-up rate. About what is its cost price?
mcqs.why: Cost price = 1,051,000 ÷ (1 + 0.35) = 1,051,000 ÷ 1.35 = Rs. 778,518.52 approximately. Divide by 1.35 to remove a 35% mark-up.

mcqs.q: A trader saves Rs. 95,000 and has goods worth Rs. 500,000. What Zakat is due?
mcqs.why: Total amount = 95,000 + 500,000 = Rs. 595,000. Zakat = 595,000 × 2.5% = Rs. 14,875. Savings and goods are added before finding Zakat.

mcqs.q: A person pays Rs. 12,500 as Zakat. On what amount did he pay it?
mcqs.why: Amount = Zakat ÷ 2.5% = 12,500 ÷ 0.025 = Rs. 500,000. Dividing the Zakat by 0.025 gives back the full amount.

mcqs.q: A farmer pays Rs. 2,000 as Ushr at the rate of 5%. What is the value of his produce?
mcqs.why: Value of produce = Ushr ÷ 5% = 2,000 ÷ 0.05 = Rs. 40,000. Work backwards from the Ushr to find the value of the produce.

lessons.title: Practical Work — Monomials, Binomials and Trinomials
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

An algebraic expression is made of terms. A term is one part joined by + or − signs. We name an expression by counting its terms.

One term means monomial. Two terms means binomial. Three terms means trinomial.

Formula / Rule

1 term = Monomial, 2 terms = Binomial, 3 terms = Trinomial.

Worked Example

Identify z² + 5z + 6.

Step 1: Split into terms: z², 5z and 6.

Step 2: Count the terms. There are 3 terms.

Step 3: So z² + 5z + 6 is a trinomial.

More Examples from the Book

−8 has only one term, so it is a monomial.

3.4 + 3.4x has two terms, 3.4 and 3.4x, so it is a binomial.

2c + 5b + 6 has three terms, so it is a trinomial.

14 + x, 5x − 2 and 4b − 2a each have two terms, so they are binomials.

Remember

  • Count terms, not letters. 5x is one term.
  • The + and − signs separate terms.
  • A single number like −8 is also a monomial.

mcqs.q: How many terms are there in 3.4 + 3.4x?
mcqs.why:
3.4 + 3.4x has two parts joined by + : 3.4 and 3.4x.
So it has 2 terms and is a binomial.
Always count the parts separated by + or −.

mcqs.q: −8 is which type of expression?
mcqs.why:
−8 is a single term with no + or − joining another term.
An expression with only one term is called a monomial.
That is why −8 is a monomial.

mcqs.q: z² + 5z + 6 is a:
mcqs.why:
The terms are z², 5z and 6 — that is 3 terms in total.
An expression with three terms is a trinomial.
So z² + 5z + 6 is a trinomial.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a binomial?
mcqs.why:
5x − 2 has two terms: 5x and −2, so it is a binomial.
−8 has one term, and the other two choices have three terms each.
Binomial always means exactly two terms.

mcqs.q: 2c + 5b + 6 has how many terms?
mcqs.why:
The terms are 2c, 5b and 6.
Counting them gives 3 terms, so it is a trinomial.
Do not count letters — count terms.

mcqs.q: 14 + x is a:
mcqs.why:
14 + x has two terms: 14 and x.
Two terms means the expression is a binomial.
A number term still counts as a term.

mcqs.q: f² + 5f + 6 is a:
mcqs.why:
f², 5f and 6 are three separate terms.
Three terms make a trinomial, just like z² + 5z + 6.
The letter used does not change the type.

mcqs.q: 4b − 2a is a binomial because:
options: It has letters b and a
mcqs.why:
4b − 2a is split by the minus sign into 4b and −2a.
That is two terms, so it is a binomial.
The reason is the number of terms, not the letters.

mcqs.q: Which expression is a monomial?
mcqs.why:
−8 stands alone as one term, so it is a monomial.
All the other choices have two terms and are binomials.
A monomial has exactly one term.

mcqs.q: 5x − 2 has terms:
mcqs.why:
In 5x − 2 the terms are 5x and −2.
The coefficient 5 belongs with x to make the term 5x.
So the expression has two terms and is a binomial.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.1 — Adding Like Terms and Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

We can add only like terms. Like terms have the same letters with the same powers, like 5a and 8a, or 9ab and −7ab. Unlike terms like a and b cannot be added together.

To add, add the numbers (coefficients) and keep the letters the same.

Formula / Rule

Add like terms: add coefficients, keep the variable part unchanged.

Worked Example

Add 5a and 8a.

Step 1: 5a and 8a are like terms.

Step 2: Add coefficients: 5 + 8 = 13.

Step 3: Keep a: 5a + 8a = 13a.

Adding Full Expressions

Collect like terms first, then add each group.

Example: (2a + 3b) + (6a + 5b) = (2a + 6a) + (3b + 5b) = 8a + 8b.

Example with x²: (6x² + 2x + 4) + (3x² + 5x) = 9x² + 7x + 4.

Decimals work the same way: 4.5a + 3.5a = 8a.

Remember

  • −12x + (−2x) = −14x. Same signs add and keep the sign.
  • 9ab + (−7ab) = 2ab. Different signs subtract.
  • Never add unlike terms: 2a + 3b stays 2a + 3b.

mcqs.why:
5a and 8a are like terms, so add the coefficients 5 + 8 = 13.
Keep the letter a unchanged: 13a.
Do not square a and do not multiply 5 × 8.

mcqs.q: a + a = ?
mcqs.why:
a means 1a, so a + a = 1a + 1a = 2a.
Adding like terms adds the hidden coefficient 1 + 1 = 2.
The answer is 2a, not a².

Both terms are negative, so add 12 + 2 = 14 and keep the minus sign.
−12x + (−2x) = −14x.
Same signs: add and keep the sign.

9ab and −7ab are like terms. 9 − 7 = 2.
So the result is 2ab.
With different signs, subtract the smaller number from the larger.

Add coefficients in order: 8 + 3 − 4 = 7.
Keep y: the answer is 7y.
Work step by step so the minus sign is not missed.

Collect like terms: a terms give 2a + 6a = 8a.
b terms give 3b + 5b = 8b.
So the sum is 8a + 8b.

x terms: 3x + 4x = 7x.
y terms: −4y + 6y = 2y.
So the sum is 7x + 2y.

Group like terms: 6x² + 3x² = 9x² and 2x + 5x = 7x.
The constant 4 has no pair, so it stays 4.
Result: 9x² + 7x + 4.

Add each letter separately: 4.5 + 3.5 = 8 for a.
5.7 + 1.3 = 7 for b, and 3.2 + 2.8 = 6 for c.
So the sum is 8a + 7b + 6c.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.2 — Subtracting Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

Subtraction also works only with like terms. When we subtract an expression in brackets, the sign of every term inside the brackets changes.

Minus times minus gives plus. So subtracting a negative term means adding.

Formula / Rule

−(a + b) = −a − b and −(a − b) = −a + b — change every sign inside.

Worked Example

Subtract 2a + 3b from 6a + 7b.

Step 1: Write (6a + 7b) − (2a + 3b).

Step 2: Subtract like terms: 6a − 2a = 4a.

Step 3: 7b − 3b = 4b.

Step 4: Answer = 4a + 4b.

Sign Care

4a − (−8a) = 4a + 8a = 12a.

(9a + 11b + 15c) − (5a + 3b − 6c): the −6c becomes +6c, so 15c + 6c = 21c.

To find what to add to get a target, do target − given expression.

Remember

  • Always change signs of the second bracket when subtracting.
  • Subtract coefficients only for like terms.
  • Check: add your answer back to the subtracted part.

mcqs.why:
Subtract like terms: 8 − 5 = 3, keep a.
8a − 5a = 3a.
Subtraction uses the coefficients only.

Both are negative like terms: −7 − 12 = −19.
So −7ab − 12ab = −19ab.
Keep the minus sign when both signs are the same.

Subtracting a negative is adding: 4a − (−8a) = 4a + 8a.
4 + 8 = 12, so the answer is 12a.
Remember: minus × minus = plus.

Subtract term by term: 6a − 2a = 4a.
7b − 3b = 4b.
So the result is 4a + 4b.

a: 9 − 5 = 4. b: 11 − 3 = 8.
c: 15c − (−6c) = 15 + 6 = 21c because the sign flips.
Result: 4a + 8b + 21c.

Rearrange by letters: c: 9c − (−5c) = 14c.
d: 8d − 4d = 4d. e: 6e − 3e = 3e.
Result: 14c + 4d + 3e.

x²: 3 − 4 = −1, so −x². ab: 25 − 18 = 7ab.
bc: 21 − (−6) = 27bc.
Result: −x² + 7ab + 27bc.

a: 5 − 4 = 1, so a. ab: 4 − 3 = 1, so ab.
b: 2b − b = b.
Result: a + ab + b.

mcqs.q: From 13a + 8b + 12c, subtract the sum of (9a + 3b + 5c) and (10a + 10b + 17c). The result is:
mcqs.why:
First add the two: 19a + 13b + 22c.
Then 13a − 19a = −6a, 8b − 13b = −5b, 12c − 22c = −10c.
Result: −6a − 5b − 10c.

mcqs.q: What should be added to 2x + 5y − 12 to get 6x + 8y?
mcqs.why:
Required = target − given = (6x + 8y) − (2x + 5y − 12).
= 4x + 3y + 12, because −(−12) = +12.
So add 4x + 3y + 12.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.3 — Multiplying Algebraic Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

In multiplication we multiply numbers with numbers and letters with letters. For the same letter, we add the powers.

For brackets, multiply every term inside by the term outside. For two brackets, multiply each term of the first by each term of the second.

Formula / Rule

aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ

(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²

Worked Example

Multiply 15a × 8a.

Step 1: Multiply numbers: 15 × 8 = 120.

Step 2: Multiply letters: a × a = a².

Step 3: Answer = 120a².

All Types in This Exercise

  • Monomial × monomial: 10a² × 2a⁵ = 20a⁷.
  • Binomial × monomial: (x − y) × (−4y) = −4xy + 4y².
  • Binomial × binomial: (3x − 2y)(2x + 5y) = 6x² + 11xy − 10y².
  • Trinomial × monomial: (2a − 3b + 4c) × 2abc = 4a²bc − 6ab²c + 8abc².
  • Trinomial × binomial: multiply each of the 3 terms by each of the 2 terms, then collect like terms.

Remember

  • Watch signs: negative × negative = positive.
  • Add powers only for the same letter.
  • Never miss a term when opening brackets.

mcqs.why:
Multiply numbers: 15 × 8 = 120.
Multiply letters: a × a = a² (add powers 1 + 1 = 2).
So 15a × 8a = 120a².

mcqs.q: 10a² × 2a⁵ = ?
mcqs.why:
Numbers: 10 × 2 = 20.
Powers of a: 2 + 5 = 7, so a⁷.
Result: 20a⁷. In multiplication we add powers, not multiply them.

Numbers: 6 × (−5) = −30. a² stays a².
b: b¹ × b² = b³. Result: −30a²b³.

Numbers: −3 × 2 × −3 = +18 (two negatives give a plus).
Letters: a × b = ab.
Result: 18ab.

Multiply both terms inside by 9: a × 9 = 9a and b × 9 = 9b.
So (a + b) × 9 = 9a + 9b.
Every term inside must be multiplied.

x × (−4y) = −4xy.
−y × (−4y) = +4y² because minus × minus = plus.
Result: −4xy + 4y².

Expand: a² − ab + ab − b². The middle terms cancel.
So (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
This is the difference of squares identity.

Multiply: 3x×2x=6x², 3x×5y=15xy, −2y×2x=−4xy, −2y×5y=−10y².
Collect xy: 15 − 4 = 11xy.
Result: 6x² + 11xy − 10y².

Multiply each term by 2abc: 2a×2abc=4a²bc.
−3b×2abc=−6ab²c and 4c×2abc=8abc².
Result: 4a²bc − 6ab²c + 8abc².

Multiply each term by 3x then by −4 and collect.
Gives 3x³ − 4x² − 15x² + 20x + 12x − 16.
Collecting: 3x³ − 19x² + 32x − 16.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.4 — Simplifying and Expanding (x + a)(x + b)
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

Simplifying means opening brackets step by step, innermost bracket first, and collecting like terms. Proving means expanding the left side until it equals the right side.

For (x + a)(x + b), the middle coefficient is a + b and the constant is a × b.

Formula / Rule

(x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab

Worked Example

Simplify 5a − 2a(3 + 4b).

Step 1: Open the bracket: 2a × 3 = 6a and 2a × 4b = 8ab.

Step 2: Write 5a − 6a − 8ab.

Step 3: Collect like terms: 5a − 6a = −a.

Step 4: Answer = −a − 8ab.

Proving (x + a)(x + b)

(x + 3)(x + 4) = x² + 4x + 3x + 12 = x² + 7x + 12.

Watch signs: (x − 5)(x − 4) = x² − 9x + 20, and (x + 2)(x − 4) = x² − 2x − 8.

For nested brackets like { } and ( ), always start from the inside.

Remember

  • A minus before a bracket changes every sign inside.
  • (2x + y)(2x − y) = 4x² − y² by difference of squares.
  • Collect like terms only at the end.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 5a − 2a(3 + 4b) = ?
mcqs.why:
Open the bracket: 2a(3 + 4b) = 6a + 8ab.
So 5a − 6a − 8ab = −a − 8ab.
First open brackets, then collect like terms.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 7m − 4m(5 − 6n) = ?
mcqs.why:
4m(5 − 6n) = 20m − 24mn.
7m − 20m + 24mn = −13m + 24mn.
Note − × − gives + for the 24mn term.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 3x − {(2x + y)(2x − y) − (4x² + 2y²)} = ?

mcqs.why:
Use (x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a+b)x + ab.
a + b = 7 and ab = 12.
So the product is x² + 7x + 12.

Middle coefficient: 5 + 6 = 11. Constant: 5 × 6 = 30.
So (x + 5)(x + 6) = x² + 11x + 30.
Add for the middle, multiply for the last term.

Here a = 2, b = −4. Sum = 2 + (−4) = −2.
Product = 2 × (−4) = −8.
So the result is x² − 2x − 8.

Sum of −3 and 4 is 1, so middle term is +x.
Product −3 × 4 = −12.
So (x − 3)(x + 4) = x² + x − 12.

Sum: −5 + (−4) = −9, so middle is −9x.
Product: (−5)(−4) = +20.
Result: x² − 9x + 20.

Sum: −7 + 8 = 1, so +x in the middle.
Product: −7 × 8 = −56.
Result: x² + x − 56.

Sum: −1 + 9 = 8, so middle term is 8x.
Product: −1 × 9 = −9.
Result: x² + 8x − 9.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.5 — Square of a Sum: (a + b)²
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

(a + b)² means (a + b) × (a + b). Its expansion always has three terms: square of first, twice the product, square of second. All signs are positive.

Formula / Rule

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

Worked Example

Prove (a + 7)² = a² + 14a + 49.

Step 1: Here a is a and b is 7.

Step 2: a² stays a².

Step 3: 2ab = 2 × a × 7 = 14a.

Step 4: b² = 7² = 49.

Step 5: So (a + 7)² = a² + 14a + 49. Proved.

More Patterns

(2x + 6)² = 4x² + 24x + 36 — remember to square 2x as (2x)² = 4x².

(3a + 5)² = 9a² + 30a + 25.

The middle term is always double: 2 × first × second.

Remember

  • Never write (a + b)² = a² + b² — the middle term 2ab is missing there.
  • Square the whole first term, including its coefficient.
  • Last term is always positive.

mcqs.why:
The identity is (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².
It has three terms: square of first, twice the product, square of second.
Forgetting 2ab is the most common mistake.

Use a² + 2ab + b² with b = 7.
2 × a × 7 = 14a and 7² = 49.
So (a + 7)² = a² + 14a + 49.

2 × a × 11 = 22a for the middle term.
11² = 121 for the last term.
So (a + 11)² = a² + 22a + 121.

Square the whole 2x: (2x)² = 4x².
Middle: 2 × 2x × 6 = 24x. Last: 6² = 36.
Result: 4x² + 24x + 36.

(3a)² = 9a². Middle: 2 × 3a × 5 = 30a.
Last: 5² = 25.
Result: 9a² + 30a + 25.

(7x)² = 49x². Middle: 2 × 7x × 3 = 42x.
Last: 3² = 9.
Result: 49x² + 42x + 9.

(6x)² = 36x². Middle: 2 × 6x × 9 = 108x.
Last: 9² = 81.
Result: 36x² + 108x + 81.

(5a)² = 25a². Middle: 2 × 5a × 4 = 40a.
Last: 4² = 16.
Result: 25a² + 40a + 16.

(9x)² = 81x². Middle: 2 × 9x × 10 = 180x.
Last: 10² = 100.
Result: 81x² + 180x + 100.

(6x)² = 36x². Middle: 2 × 6x × 7 = 84x.
Last: 7² = 49.
Result: 36x² + 84x + 49.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.6 — Square of a Difference: (a − b)²
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

This is like (a + b)², but the middle term is negative because we subtract. The first and last terms are still positive squares.

Formula / Rule

(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

Worked Example

Prove (a − 3)² = a² − 6a + 9.

Step 1: Here b is 3.

Step 2: a² stays a².

Step 3: −2ab = −2 × a × 3 = −6a.

Step 4: b² = 3² = 9 (positive).

Step 5: So (a − 3)² = a² − 6a + 9. Proved.

Key Difference from (a + b)²

(2a − 5)² = 4a² − 20a + 25 — only the middle sign changes.

(6x − 8)² = 36x² − 96x + 64.

Remember

  • Last term is always +b², never negative.
  • Middle term: −2 × first × second.
  • Square the whole first term: (4a)² = 16a².

mcqs.why:
The identity is (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
Only the middle term is negative.
The last term b² is always positive.

Middle: −2 × a × 3 = −6a. Last: 3² = +9.
So (a − 3)² = a² − 6a + 9.
Remember the last term stays positive.

Middle: −2 × a × 7 = −14a.
Last: 7² = 49.
Result: a² − 14a + 49.

(2a)² = 4a². Middle: −2 × 2a × 5 = −20a.
Last: 5² = 25.
Result: 4a² − 20a + 25.

(6x)² = 36x². Middle: −2 × 6x × 8 = −96x.
Last: 8² = 64.
Result: 36x² − 96x + 64.

(4a)² = 16a². Middle: −2 × 4a × 7 = −56a.
Last: 7² = 49.
Result: 16a² − 56a + 49.

(3a)² = 9a². Middle: −2 × 3a × 8 = −48a.
Last: 8² = 64.
Result: 9a² − 48a + 64.

(7a)² = 49a². Middle: −2 × 7a × 5 = −70a.
Last: 5² = 25.
Result: 49a² − 70a + 25.

(9a)² = 81a². Middle: −2 × 9a × 11 = −198a.
Last: 11² = 121, always positive.
Result: 81a² − 198a + 121.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.7 — Difference of Squares: (a + b)(a − b)
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

When the same two terms appear once with + and once with −, the middle terms cancel. Only the squares remain, with a minus between them.

Formula / Rule

(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²

a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

Worked Example

Prove (3x + 2)(3x − 2) = 9x² − 4.

Step 1: Here a is 3x and b is 2.

Step 2: Square the first: (3x)² = 9x².

Step 3: Square the second: 2² = 4.

Step 4: Subtract: 9x² − 4. Proved.

Both Directions

Expanding: (5x + 4)(5x − 4) = 25x² − 16.

Factorising: 4a² − 9b² = (2a + 3b)(2a − 3b).

64m² − 81 = (8m + 9)(8m − 9).

Remember

  • There is NO middle term in the answer.
  • Square the whole term: (10q)² = 100q².
  • This works only for a difference (−), not a sum of squares.

mcqs.why:
Expanding gives a² − ab + ab − b², and the middle terms cancel.
So (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
This is the difference of squares identity.

a = 3x, b = 2. (3x)² = 9x² and 2² = 4.
Subtract: 9x² − 4.
No middle term remains.

(4x)² = 16x² and 3² = 9.
So the product is 16x² − 9.
Use a² − b² directly.

(5x)² = 25x² and 4² = 16.
Difference: 25x² − 16.
The answer is a difference, so the sign is minus.

(6x)² = 36x² and 5² = 25.
So (6x + 5)(6x − 5) = 36x² − 25.
Square each whole term first.

(7x)² = 49x² and 6² = 36.
Subtract: 49x² − 36.
This uses (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

mcqs.q: 4a² − 9b² factorises as:
mcqs.why:
4a² = (2a)² and 9b² = (3b)², so it is a difference of squares.
a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) gives (2a + 3b)(2a − 3b).
Read the identity in reverse to factorise.

64m² = (8m)² and 81 = 9².
So 64m² − 81 = (8m + 9)(8m − 9).
Find the square roots of both terms.

√(9p²) = 3p and √(100q²) = 10q.
Difference of squares gives (3p + 10q)(3p − 10q).
One bracket has +, the other has −.

100y² = (10y)² and 169 = 13².
So it factorises as (10y + 13)(10y − 13).
Check: 13 × 13 = 169.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.8 — Factorising by Taking Out a Common Factor
lessons.notes_html:
The Main Idea

Factorising is the reverse of expanding. First look for a factor common to every term — a number, a letter, or a whole bracket — and take it outside.

Formula / Rule

ab + ac = a(b + c) — take the common factor a outside the bracket.

Worked Example

Factorise 5a²x − 15a.

Step 1: Common factor of 5a²x and 15a is 5a.

Step 2: Divide each term by 5a: 5a²x ÷ 5a = ax, 15a ÷ 5a = 3.

Step 3: Write 5a(ax − 3).

Harder Cases

m⁴ − m³ + m² = m²(m² − m + 1) — take the lowest power.

a²bc + ab²c + abc² = abc(a + b + c).

A bracket can be the common factor: 3a(b + c) + 6d(b + c) = 3(b + c)(a + 2d).

Remember

  • Take the HCF — highest common factor — of all terms.
  • Check by expanding your answer back.
  • Do not forget the 1 when a term becomes empty, e.g. m² ÷ m² = 1.

mcqs.q: Factorise: 5a²x − 15a = ?
mcqs.why:
The HCF of 5a²x and 15a is 5a.
Dividing gives ax and 3 inside the bracket.
So 5a²x − 15a = 5a(ax − 3).

mcqs.q: Factorise: m⁴ − m³ + m² = ?
mcqs.why:
Every term contains m², the lowest power.
Divide each term by m²: m², −m, +1.
Result: m²(m² − m + 1). Note the last term becomes 1.

mcqs.q: Factorise: 7a³ + 14a² − 7 = ?
mcqs.why:
The common factor is 7.
14a² ÷ 7 = 2a² and −7 ÷ 7 = −1.
Result: 7(a³ + 2a² − 1).

mcqs.q: Factorise: mx² − m²x − mx = ?
mcqs.why:
Common factor of all three terms is mx.
Dividing: x, −m, −1.
Result: mx(x − m − 1).

mcqs.q: Factorise: a²bc + ab²c + abc² = ?
mcqs.why:
